findings.title: Reuse drift assertions through a helper, not pytest test functions
findings.problem: The parameterized release-version test invokes two functions whose names and signatures identify them as pytest tests, and temporarily replaces the module-level `load_validator` function so those test bodies use its fixture. This couples one test to other test entry points and their signatures instead of expressing reusable assertions directly.
findings.current_code:
monkeypatch.setattr(sys.modules[__name__], "load_validator", lambda: validator)
with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
    test_release_please_config_rejects_version_seed_drift(patch, cases)
for target, filename, field in (...):
    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
        test_release_please_config_rejects_consumer_version_drift(
            patch, cases, target, filename, field
        )
findings.suggested_fix: Extract fixture setup and drift assertions into ordinary helpers with explicit validator and temporary-directory parameters. Call those helpers from both standalone pytest cases and the multi-version test, without replacing the module-level loader.
findings.post_review_resolution: Addressed after the reviewed snapshot: assert_version_seed_drift_rejected and assert_consumer_version_drift_rejected now contain the reusable assertions. Pytest cases and the multi-version test call these helpers with an explicit validator; the module-level loader is no longer monkeypatched.

positive_changes: New regression tests generally use explicit expected values and temporary fixtures, keeping important expectations independent of production-derived values.
The shared native-tool fixtures scope local skips and hosted failures to the relevant integrations; README guidance explains the distinction.
The README and changes record avoid representing locally skipped integrations as passed hosted evidence.
testing_recommendations: Obtain the provisioned hosted Python 3.12/native-tool/official-SPDX run recorded as pending before describing integrations as fully validated.
